newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac denounces "conspiracy of silence" on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Chirac denounces "conspiracy of silence" on Zaire.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, denouncing a "conspiracy of silence" on Zaire, appealed to the international community on Tuesday to force a ceasefire in the African state and take emergency humanitarian action.

Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said Chirac told a cabinet meeting: "The humanitarian situation in Zaire is tragic. No one can ignore it any longer. No one can remain indifferent. We have to ask if there is not a sort of conspiracy of silence."

Rebels fighting the government of French-backed President Mobutu Sese Seko have captured a swathe of eastern Zaire, driving Rwandan Hutu refugees before them, and now threaten the key garrison city of Kisangani on the Zaire river.

"France appeals solemnly to the international community to take responsibility by exerting the necessary pressure to obtain a ceasefire and to implement urgently needed humanitarian intervention," Chirac was quoted as saying.
He said France strongly supported proposals by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan for an international humanitarian intervention force.

Emergency Humanitarian Aid Minister Xavier Emmanuelli, just back from Zaire, reported to the cabinet that the refugee situation was "very somber" and proposed that France launch its own mini-airlift while awaiting wider international support.
